operatingIdea: Force complete resolution inside a precisely bounded problem world.
bestFor: A sharply defined frontier problem where partial progress, evasion, or equivalent restatement must not count.
produces: A complete candidate resolution subjected to counterexample search, boundary checks, and an explicit irreparable-blocker condition.
antiUseCases: Do not use when the problem boundary, evidence access, or success condition is genuinely open-ended.
representativeRequest: Use Closed-World Grand Challenge to mathematical proof with explicit evidence and acceptance gates.
applicabilityGate: Confirm that the requested object, governing rules, available evidence, and completion condition form a genuinely closed problem world.
Treat missing but obtainable inputs as repairable underdetermination, not as an irreparable blocker; identify the smallest input contract that would close the world.
Never replace the requested object with a meta-compliance exercise or mark completion from self-invented premises, tests, or evidence.
observableOutputContract: A normalized closed-world statement with explicit objects, rules, evidence, and completion claims.
At least one substantive candidate resolution, or the strongest conditional candidate when repairable inputs are missing.
Counterexample and boundary results tied to the candidate's exact claims.
A final COMPLETE, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED, or NOT_APPLICABLE status whose evidence is stated explicitly.
solExecutionContract: Run the applicability gate first. Define every supplied object and boundary needed to make the problem closed; do not silently invent missing premises or redefine the requested object.
Assume for search purposes that a complete valid resolution exists, without treating that assumption as evidence or as permission to assert the conclusion.
Enumerate the exact claims that constitute completion and the plausible-looking partial results that do not count.
Develop materially different candidate routes, preserve independence long enough to expose real strengths, and block any route that merely renames the central difficulty.
Search aggressively for counterexamples, circularity, hidden assumptions, degenerate cases, and failures at the task boundary.
When inputs are repairably incomplete, produce the strongest substantive conditional candidate plus the exact minimal input contract needed to verify it; do not collapse into a generic plan.

Return COMPLETE only for a verified resolution, CONDITIONAL for an evidence-bounded candidate, BLOCKED only for a supported external impediment, or NOT_APPLICABLE when the world cannot legitimately be closed.
failureAndAdversarialChecklist: Reject requirement loss, unsupported claims, fabricated evidence, or unapproved authority expansion.
Test boundary cases, counterexamples, failure modes, and the strongest plausible rejected alternative.
Require observable acceptance evidence and state unresolved uncertainty explicitly.
Do not use when the problem boundary, evidence access, or success condition is genuinely open-ended.

profileAdaptations.single: One Sol agent owns synthesis and uses independent internal passes without claiming nonexistent agents.
profileAdaptations.multi: Delegate only genuinely independent bounded workstreams; preserve provenance, handoffs, integration tests, and root synthesis.
profileAdaptations.ultra: Production Ultra uses full_approved_capsule semantics only after a signed and verified native capability attestation and user authorization bind the canonical capsule, complete budget, kill switch, and lease policy plus branch termination and root acceptance; proof_only is a development and validation mode, never the production default.
